summary.text: Analilia Mejia is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District, elected in an April 2026 special election to succeed Mikie Sherrill after Sherrill became governor. She has worked as a labor and political organizer, including as director of the New Jersey Working Families Alliance, deputy director of the U.S. Department of Labor's Women's Bureau, and national political director of Sen. Bernie Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign. She sits on the Homeland Security and Small Business committees and is seeking a full term.

paragraphs.text: Born August 19, 1977, in Elizabeth, New Jersey, and raised in New Jersey, the daughter of Colombian and Dominican immigrants. Her official biography says her mother worked as a seamstress and that the family's finances changed when her mother got a union job.
Earned a bachelor's degree in comparative literature (2000), a Master of Public Policy (2002), and a master's in labor relations and education (2003), all at Rutgers University-New Brunswick.

Began her career as a union organizer; Wikipedia lists her as an organizer with the United Food and Commercial Workers, political director of SEIU Local 32BJ, and assistant political director at UNITE HERE in Chicago.

Was Latino and labor vote director for Sen. Bob Menendez's 2012 re-election campaign, and from 2014 served as director of the New Jersey Working Families Alliance, where her official biography says she led campaigns for a $15 minimum wage and paid sick leave.
Was a delegate for Bernie Sanders in the 2016 Democratic presidential primary and left the Working Families Alliance in 2019 to become national political director of his 2020 presidential campaign.
Served as deputy director of the Women's Bureau at the U.S. Department of Labor during the Biden administration, then as co-executive director of the Center for Popular Democracy.

Announced her candidacy for the special election on November 25, 2025, after Mikie Sherrill won the governorship. She won the February 5, 2026 special Democratic primary with 29.3% in an 11-candidate field, then defeated Joe Hathaway (R) and Alan Bond (independent) in the April 16, 2026 special general election with 60.2% of the vote.
Sworn into the House on April 20, 2026, and assigned to the Homeland Security and Small Business committees. She has introduced legislation to raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour.
Her official biography says she lives in Glen Ridge and is a mother.
